feature: Product robustness: collision-free UI, automatic resilient agent connection, dependable scene import/export, and higher-accuracy agent design guidance

seams.what: the fixed top bar that independently positions run, status, settings, file, and connection controls
seams.evidence: run controls are absolutely positioned inside a full-width fixed panel while connection controls use a separate fixed positioning system
seams.asks: which controls must remain visible at narrow widths, and which may collapse into an overflow menu?

seams.what: the top-right connection control that can occupy the same space as run and settings controls
seams.evidence: the button is fixed to a top-right inset without participating in the top bar layout
seams.asks: should connection state live as a compact status in the top bar or as an action inside the settings area?

seams.what: the three-row sidebar layout shared by chat, selected-object controls, and logs
seams.evidence: the selected-object row has a fixed 152px allocation although it now contains texture controls as well as transforms
seams.asks: how much persistent space should chat, object editing, and logs each receive, and which sections may collapse?

seams.what: the selected-object inspector body that contains transform and texture editing
seams.evidence: the growing body has no bounded scrolling while its parent clips overflow
seams.asks: should long object controls scroll in place, expand the sidebar row, or use collapsible sections?

seams.what: the texture editor styling inside the selected-object panel
seams.evidence: the stylesheet expects BEM-named descendants while the rendered markup uses texture-presets, texture-maps, and texture-transform classes
seams.asks: which texture controls should be immediately visible and which advanced controls should be collapsed by default?

seams.what: the application startup point for agent-client detection and connection status
seams.evidence: startup only installs a click handler; client detection and configuration do not run until the user clicks
seams.asks: should startup only detect and report clients, or also rewrite detected clients' MCP configuration files automatically?

seams.what: detection and configuration of Codex, Claude, and Cursor clients
seams.evidence: the backend can identify configured clients and write their external config, but newly written Codex configuration still requires a client restart
seams.asks: which external client files may Forge3D modify without a click, and how should restart-required state be communicated?

seams.what: the user-facing save, open, import, and export workflow
seams.evidence: the menu submits jobs while scene-replacing operations are forbidden during a running agent session, leaving the failure to appear after submission
seams.asks: should scene-changing operations auto-pause and remain paused, or require the user to pause before choosing a file?

seams.what: the asynchronous job runner used for file operations
seams.evidence: real Blender export fails because bpy operators are invoked from this worker thread instead of Blender's owning thread
seams.asks: should file work remain visibly asynchronous with progress and cancellation while Blender execution is marshalled safely to its owning thread?

seams.what: the live composition root connecting browser file jobs to Blender-backed operations
seams.evidence: the HTTP server creates a generic threaded job manager even though the live engine has thread affinity
seams.asks: should the browser keep receiving job ids and progress while all Blender mutations are serialized with agent commands?

seams.what: the application callback that turns an export request into a downloadable artifact
seams.evidence: it delegates directly to the Blender exporter from whichever thread executes the file job
seams.asks: should export default to the whole scene or the current selection, and what should users receive when one requested format is unsupported?

seams.what: the real Blender glTF/GLB operator whose context and thread requirements determine whether export succeeds
seams.evidence: a live GLB export reproducibly fails inside Blender because the worker thread has no active-object context
seams.asks: which production formats must have real-Blender round-trip guarantees rather than mock-only coverage?

seams.what: the catalogue of tools exposed to an agent in every MCP list-tools response
seams.evidence: the current bridge flattens all role registries, so the agent sees 52 tools even though the architecture describes a smaller phase-specific surface
seams.asks: should agents see only orientation plus the tools legal for the current design phase, or keep the entire catalogue visible?

seams.anchor: def build_server(sdk: SdkModules, orchestrator: Any, *, name: str, version: str) -> Any:
seams.what: the MCP server construction point where concise workflow instructions can guide every connected agent
seams.evidence: the installed MCP SDK supports server instructions, but Forge3D currently supplies none
seams.asks: which accuracy loop should be mandatory: orient, construct semantically, inspect measurements, correct reported problems, then promote?

seams.anchor: def build_registry(*, include_raw: bool = True) -> dict[ToolRole, tuple[ToolSpec, ...]]:
seams.what: the role partitions and catalogue-size policy used to guide tool choice
seams.evidence: the registry warns that blockout and refine exceed the intended accuracy band but deliberately keeps the oversized lists
seams.asks: may this robustness pass supersede the earlier decision to keep every legal tool visible when that reduces agent selection accuracy?

seams.what: the orientation tool agents are already told to call before editing
seams.evidence: its description says to call it first, but no server-level instruction or evaluation verifies that agents follow the workflow
seams.asks: what minimum context and next-action guidance should agents receive before they can mutate a scene?

seams.what: the rendered-layout regression suite for narrow viewports and control collisions
seams.evidence: it checks run controls against status at 529px but does not check connection, settings, file, or sidebar inspector collisions
seams.asks: what is the smallest supported desktop width, and should controls collapse before any overlap is possible?

seams.anchor: test('File menu exposes native project/model actions and keeps the dialog named', async () => {
seams.what: the rendered browser coverage for file menu actions and state
seams.evidence: the browser test verifies labels and dialog accessibility but not a real save/open/import/export round trip
seams.asks: which complete file journeys must be verified through the UI before this feature is considered dependable?

seams.what: the HTTP integration tests for live project and model jobs
seams.evidence: the test uses a fake engine, so it cannot detect Blender thread-affinity failures seen in the live application
seams.asks: should CI include a small real-Blender file round trip in addition to fast fake-engine coverage?

seams.anchor: node .pipeline/check.mjs             # the gate — reads disk, re-runs both suites
seams.what: the documented whole-project verification command agents are expected to run
seams.evidence: the documented gate currently fails because .pipeline/check.mjs is absent, allowing agents to stop without the promised cross-suite check
seams.asks: should one restored command verify backend, frontend, browser availability, wiring, and feature state with clear skipped-versus-failed reporting?
